requirements.quote: Each runbook has the required headings (Purpose, Triggers, Roles, Steps, Communications, Evidence, Verification, After action), an owner and a `Last drilled` date; a CI check fails otherwise [type:unit]

The CERT-In runbook defines the 6-hour clock from detection, lists incident categories in the directions, and includes a ready report template and an evidence checklist referencing the 180-day India log store [type:manual]
`evidence-export.sh` exports logs for a time range from Loki into an encrypted archive within India, with a manifest and hash, and is tested against seeded logs [type:api]

The DPDP runbook covers assessment, containment, Board and principal notification as applicable, customer (Data Fiduciary) notification templates, and record keeping; counsel-owned sections are marked `Counsel to confirm` until the human issue is complete [type:manual]

The key rotation runbook covers KEK rotation with DEK re-wrap without downtime, session secret and API secret rotation, SSH and deploy key rotation, backup encryption key rotation and an emergency compromise path; each step has a verification command [type:manual]
`rotate-kek.sh` is exercised in CI against staging-like data: after rotation all documents still decrypt and the old KEK is rejected [type:api]
The restore and DR runbooks match the measured RPO and RTO from #101 drills and link to the latest drill report [type:manual]

The on-call runbook defines severities P0 to P3, response targets, escalation ladder, handoff and a communication plan including the public status page and WhatsApp support line during court-day hours [type:manual]
A tabletop drill is held for CERT-In and DPDP scenarios, and a technical drill for restore and key rotation, with records saved under `drills/` before launch [type:manual]
requirements.why: Drills need humans (participants, a live staging restore and key rotation) and are due before launch, not at merge. This change ships drills/TEMPLATE.md, one pending record per runbook and a README launch checklist; the engine files the follow-up to hold the drills and fill the records.

requirements.quote: Runbooks contain no secrets or real personal data; a secret scanner runs on `infra/runbooks/` in CI [type:unit]
Runbooks state that no automated outbound messages go to courts or third parties and that customer notices are sent by a human after approval, consistent with the no auto-send guardrail [type:manual]
These are documents with drills, not decoration: each runbook is exercised in a tabletop or technical drill before launch and the evidence is stored.
requirements.why: Same as R9: executing the drills is a pre-launch human activity; the template and pending records are delivered here.

decisions.choice: No new workspace dependency; rotate-kek.ts imports @causedeck/storage and @causedeck/config via the existing workspace resolution (script run with pnpm --filter <pkg> exec tsx); the CI proof is a vitest inside packages/storage
decisions.justification: rewrapAll already exists (packages/storage/src/workspace-crypto.ts:158); rotation.test.ts:1-30 is the DB-backed precedent; tsx is only in db/auth/ui (db/package.json:52), so the wrapper runs through the db package, which storage already depends on
